papers.title_en: Generative Translation Priors: Bayesian Imaging with Cross-Modality Image Translation
papers.authors: Evan Bell, Jiaming Liu, Yifan Chen, Yu Sun
papers.evidence: 将翻译模型转化为逆问题先验的通用贝叶斯框架，可应用于EEG源成像
papers.tldr: 成像反问题中常可获取共注册的交叉模态图像，但现有方法难以将其作为先验信息。本文提出生成式翻译先验（GTP），将基于扩散的图像翻译模型转化为贝叶斯框架下的跨模态先验，通过似然引导推动采样趋向目标后验分布。理论分析了引导带来的固有偏差，并推导了无需真值的偏差估计指标。进一步给出梯度与近端两种离散化算法，在CT/MR和PET/CT重建任务上验证了其有效整合互补信息的能力，即使在严重欠采样下也能实现高保真重建。
papers.abstract_en: The ability to leverage images from co-available modalities to inform target-domain reconstruction is highly desirable in imaging algorithms. In this work, we introduce Generative Translation Priors (GTP)--a Bayesian framework that transforms diffusion-based image-to-image translation models into cross-modality image priors for ill-posed imaging inverse problems. GTP incorporates target-domain measurements through likelihood guidance, steering the translation process toward the desired posterior distribution. The framework is grounded in a theoretical analysis of the resulting posterior dynamics, which reveals an intrinsic bias introduced by likelihood guidance. We further characterize this bias and derive a ground-truth-free formulation for its estimation, enabling it to serve as a practical metric for assessing posterior sampling quality. Building on this analysis, we derive two discretized GTP algorithms based on gradient and proximal likelihood guidance, respectively. We validate GTP on computed tomography reconstruction with magnetic resonance side information, and on positron emission tomography reconstruction with computed tomography side information. Experiments demonstrate that GTP effectively incorporates complementary cross-modality information and achieves high-fidelity reconstruction even under severely undersampled measurements.
